blocks.text: Design the browser side of a short-video feed where one settled card owns playback, directional preload stays bounded, and rapid swipes cannot leak media work.

blocks.title: Use RADIO
blocks.text: Requirements define the user journey, device and network constraints, playback policy, failure behavior, and measurable success criteria before architecture decisions are made.

What you are solving:
An endless short-video feed with instant playback, responsive scrolling, and predictable controls. The UI must stay smooth across device classes while handling variable networks, long sessions, and bursty user behavior (fast swipes).

Decision surface:
- Fast first play and prefetch strategy
- Handling variable networks and devices
- Virtualization + memory control
- Playback lifecycle (only one active player)
- CDN rendition selection and caching
- UI performance budgets and observability

steps.title: 1) Open feed
steps.text: Fetch the first page of metadata, render the first card, and show a poster immediately.

steps.title: 2) Fast first play
steps.text: Preconnect to CDN, request video metadata, and start playback for the first visible card.

steps.title: 3) Prefetch next items
steps.text: Prepare a measured directional neighbor window based on settled intent, swipe velocity, cache evidence, device memory, and network or Save-Data signals.

steps.title: 4) Rapid scroll
steps.text: Pause offscreen videos, cancel in-flight downloads, and keep only one active decoder.

steps.title: 5) Slow network
steps.text: Downshift quality, show a buffering UI, and resume when bandwidth recovers.

blocks.title: Clarifying questions
items: How many videos should be prefetched?
Should videos autoplay on cellular by default?
Do we need offline or data-saver modes?

blocks.title: Non-functional expectations
items: A smooth scroll and snap experience on the supported device matrix, verified with field frame data.
Time-to-first-frame budgets segmented by device and network class, then revised from production percentiles.
Bounded memory usage over long sessions.
Consistent UI across regions and devices.

items.label: Time to first frame
items.helperText: Set a starting hypothesis per device and network class.

items.label: Prefetch window
items.helperText: Tune from swipe velocity, memory, Save-Data, and connection evidence.

items.label: Scroll budget
items.helperText: Profile interaction work instead of assuming one universal frame budget.

blocks.title: Critical trade-off
blocks.text: More prefetching can improve the next start, but it increases memory and bandwidth. Justify the policy with measured startup and abandonment data, and cancel obsolete priority work after rapid scroll.

blocks.title: Explicit assumptions
items: Autoplay, codec, reduced-motion, and inline-playback support across target devices.
Rendition coverage for viewport sizes, Save-Data users, and constrained connections.
Swipe velocity, session length, and low-memory pressure that shape the preload window.
First-frame, rebuffer, and interaction budgets segmented by device and network cohort.

blocks.title: Playback success measures
rows: Separates page rendering from playback startup

blocks.text: The client controls viewport intent, active-player ownership, media element reuse, preload cancellation, memory pressure, and playback UI. Server-side ranking, encoding, and recommendation stay behind abstract feed contracts; CDN topology and origin selection stay behind abstract media-delivery contracts.
